steps.label: CLI knowledge silhouette-readability

response.title: Evaluate identity using silhouette and target backgrounds
requires: Intended viewing scale, representative backgrounds and identity landmarks
procedure: Render a flat opaque mask before detailing.
Inspect major proportions, negative spaces and landmark separation at native logical scale.
Compare the colored asset on representative light, dark and busy backgrounds.
checks: Named identity landmarks remain visible at the target size.
Required gaps stay open and interactive forms separate from their surroundings.
pitfalls: Silhouette alone cannot validate faces, materials or fine symbols.
No contrast ratio or component count proves aesthetic quality.

procedure: Draw a 16x16 key with a ring hole, shaft and two teeth; render mask and colored views on three backgrounds.
Create a negative example by filling the hole and merging the teeth.
acceptance: Record native-scale contact sheets and explicit pass/fail for hole, shaft and both teeth.
Negative example fails the landmark checklist; aesthetic review remains separate.

steps.label: CLI knowledge dither-coverage

response.title: Count dither coverage and constrain its region
requires: A tileable threshold matrix, two approved colors and a region mask
procedure: For fraction q, select cells with rank < 16*q when 16*q is integral.
Keep the pattern phase consistent across adjacent regions unless a discontinuity is intentional.
checks: Coverage is the actual selected-cell count divided by total cells.
The pattern changes only within its semantic mask.
pitfalls: The local source's example percentage labels are incorrect; count cells instead.
Dither can add noise and is optional; flat clusters may suit an asset better.

procedure: Threshold the specified 4x4 matrix at 4, 8 and 12.
Tile each result 3x3 and inspect coverage and boundary continuation.
acceptance: Selected populations are exactly 4, 8 and 12 of 16.

The two supplied dither passages repeat the same example and are not independent corroboration.

instruction_revision_review.scope: Read-only review of the revised Failures and recovery table; no repeated production scenario, copied runtime calls or bundle recopy.

reviewed_range.text:
| Observation | Required response |
| --- | --- |
| Discovery reports a missing inventory/source or an inventory hash/line-count mismatch | Preserve the diagnostic and stop dependent adoption. In a development task, repair provenance deliberately; in a production task, report the unusable installation/source and continue unrelated work. |
| Exact retrieval rejects a stale expected hash, but fresh source discovery validates the installed revision | Retain the rejected attempt. Re-read the current method and its context, then retrieve its current citation with the matching inventory identity. Never carry an old revision's line range into a new file merely by replacing the hash. If discovery also fails, use the installation-conflict response above. |
| Citation outside the declared source or range | Do not guess a replacement paragraph. Check the actual method/source revision and correct the citation through an explicit source review. |
| Source budget exceeded | Narrow to a meaningful cited section or increase the explicit budget; do not present a truncated result as the complete citation. |
| Stale compiled context or proof receipt | Do not recompute hashes on the old receipt. Re-execute applicable checks and compile updated evidence through the development workflow. |
| Local research contains historical citation tokens or unsupported attribution | Retain its stated status. Verify consequential external claims against retrievable primary sources before using them as current facts. |
| Method requires unavailable tooling or engine access | Keep the method as researched knowledge and name the missing proof. A fixture or prepared request cannot stand in for the unavailable operation. |

instruction_revision_review.reason: The table now distinguishes a failing inventory/source installation from a rejected stale expectation with fresh successful discovery. Recovery preserves the failure, re-reads the current method/context, and retrieves its current citation with the matching identity. It explicitly forbids carrying an old range into a new revision by only replacing the hash and falls back to the installation-conflict response when discovery fails.
instruction_revision_review.behavior_validation: Not rerun. The revised wording was not part of the original copied-snapshot execution, and this review establishes only that it resolves the reported textual ambiguity.
